subtopic: CUDA / Race conditions on shared memory
learningObjective: Identify a race condition in a CUDA kernel that writes and reads shared memory without adequate synchronization.
stem: The kernel below is intended to compute `y[tid] = x[tid-1] + x[tid]` (with `y[0] = x[0]`) using shared memory. Identify the correctness issue.

options.text: The write `smem[tid] = x[tid]` is atomic per lane, so no synchronization is needed; the CUDA runtime automatically inserts a barrier before any subsequent shared-memory read.

There is no race because thread `tid` only reads `smem[tid]` and `smem[tid - 1]`; both writes come from thread `tid - 1` and thread `tid`, which are in the same warp for `tid < 32` and therefore execute in lockstep.
The kernel is incorrect because `__shared__ float smem[256]` requires an explicit `__syncthreads()` at kernel entry to initialize the shared memory to zero.

Without a `__syncthreads()` between the write `smem[tid] = x[tid]` and the read `smem[tid - 1]`, there is a race: thread `tid` may read `smem[tid - 1]` before thread `tid - 1` has written it. The fix is to insert `__syncthreads()` immediately after the shared-memory store.

explanation: Classic SMEM race: writes by different threads (`smem[tid] = x[tid]`) must be visible before any thread reads a value written by a different thread (`smem[tid - 1]`). Without `__syncthreads()`, thread `tid` may reach the read before thread `tid - 1` has performed its write, producing undefined values. Lockstep-within-warp is not sufficient on Volta+ (ITS) and not guaranteed as a portable assumption; the correct fix is `__syncthreads()`. Choice C fabricates a zero-init requirement; SMEM is uninitialized. Choice D denies the shared-memory data race.

optionExplanations.D: Correct: missing __syncthreads causes SMEM read-before-write race.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: lockstep-within-warp is not portable; and cross-warp reads still race.
optionExplanations.A: Wrong: no automatic barrier is inserted.

assumptions: Modern NVIDIA GPU with ITS behavior.
nonImplications: Does not imply all missing __syncthreads always produce wrong results; small blocks may seem to work by accident.
Does not imply __syncthreads is a memory fence for global memory; it is per-block SMEM/register fence.
